title: Cube net with opposite-face number sums
observableEvidence: Folds a cube net mentally to identify which three pairs of squares become opposite faces, then uses a shared-sum condition across those pairs to solve for an unknown face value.
prompt: A cube net has square P in the center, Q directly above P, R directly below P, S directly left of P, T directly right of P, and U attached directly above Q. The six squares are labeled with the numbers 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 13, one per square: P = 9, Q = 13, R = 7, S = 12, and T = 8, and U has the one remaining number. When the net is folded into a cube, every pair of opposite faces has the same sum. What number is on face U?

contestFormat.eligibility: Grade 8 or below and age 15.5 years or younger on the official contest date.

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.rationale: Assumes Q, the square touching P in the net, is opposite P instead of R, and computes 20 - 13 = 7 using the wrong neighbor as the opposite face.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.rationale: Correct: Q and R are directly in line through the center (Q-P-R), so they fold to opposite faces, giving the shared sum 13 + 7 = 20. Since P and U are also directly in line (U-Q-P), P and U are opposite too, so U = 20 - 9 = 11.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.rationale: Assumes every arm of the net folds the same way and copies S's value (12) for U, without checking which pair is actually opposite P.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.rationale: Loses track of the fold direction from Q to U and copies U = Q = 13, instead of recognizing that U folds to the far side, opposite P.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.rationale: Reports the shared opposite-face sum itself (20) instead of finishing the last step of solving for U.

solutionRepresentation: In the net, Q and R sit directly above and below P in a straight line (Q-P-R), so when folded they become opposite faces; their sum is 13 + 7 = 20, which is the constant sum for every opposite pair. U and Q and P are also in a straight line (U-Q-P), so U is opposite P, giving U = 20 - 9 = 11. (As a check, S and T are also opposite: 12 + 8 = 20, confirming the shared sum.)
solutionMethod: Use the net's straight-line arrangement of three squares to identify which pairs fold to opposite faces, then use the shared opposite-face sum to solve for the unknown value.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept the number alone, as U = 11, or as choice B.

hintSteps.prompt: Look for three squares in a straight line in the net; the two outer squares in that line become opposite faces when folded.
hintSteps.question: Which two squares are in a straight line with U in between it and P?

hintSteps.prompt: Use a pair of opposite faces whose numbers you already know to find the shared sum every opposite pair must have.
hintSteps.question: What do Q and R add up to, and what does that tell you about every opposite pair?

hintSteps.prompt: If two known opposite faces add to 20, and the pair you need includes a face labeled 9, the unknown face is 20 minus 9.
hintSteps.question: Which answer choice equals the shared sum minus P's number?
